readout_other: Motor-evoked potential (MEP) amplitude, short- and long-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI/LICI), intracortical facilitation (ICF), and cortical silent period (cSP) via single/paired-pulse TMS-EMG
direction_notes: Sonication at 12 W/cm2 ISPPA significantly increased MEP amplitude; TUS at 6, 9, and 12 W/cm2 significantly shortened cortical silent period (cSP). No significant change to SICI, LICI, or ICF at any intensity.
safety_notes: During the experiment, one participant reported mild, transient distending pain over the right frontal region during the 9 W/cm2 sonication, which resolved spontaneously after 3 min rest period. No other adverse events were reported.

exposures.label: Active TUS to M1 hotspot (ISPPA 3, 6, 9, 12 W/cm2)

device.manufacturer: GreenValley BrainTech Medical Technology Co. Ltd.

timing.protocol_description: Pulse Duration (PD) = 0.3 ms, Pulse Repetition Interval (PRI) = 5 ms, Pulse Train Duration (PTD) = 1 s, Inter-Stimulus Interval (ISI) = 5 s, Sonication Period (SP) = 6 s, PRF = 200 Hz, DC = 6%. Each 1-s pulse train was delivered every 6 s, with total sonication delivered for 20 minutes per session.

source_quotes.n_subjects: A total of twenty-five healthy, right-handed subjects (19 females, 6 males; mean age ± standard deviation = 24.0 ± 3.3 years, range = 21–30 years) recruited from Shanghai Yangzhi Rehabilitation Hospital participated in this study.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Each participant completed five experimental sessions, corresponding to four active ISPPA levels (3, 6, 9, and 12 W/cm<sup>2</sup> in the free-field) and one sham condition.
